q01.key_idea: Find the number that sits inside all three shapes at the same time.
steps: Look for the spot where the circle, the square and the triangle all cover each other.
The 5 is inside the circle, inside the square and inside the triangle.
Every other number is outside at least one of the shapes.

choice_feedback.A: The 1 is only inside the circle.
choice_feedback.B: The 4 is inside the circle and the triangle, but not inside the square.
choice_feedback.D: The 9 is only inside the triangle.
choice_feedback.E: There is no 12 in the picture.

q02.key_idea: Use the lines behind the pencils like a ruler and count the spaces each pencil covers.
steps: The lines behind the pencils are all the same distance apart, so we can count spaces.
From its back end to its tip, pencil A covers about 6 spaces, B about 8, C about 7, D about 9 and E about 8.
Pencil D covers the most spaces, so it is the longest.

choice_feedback.A: Pencil A covers only about 6 spaces. It is the shortest.
choice_feedback.B: Pencil B covers about 8 spaces. Pencil D covers 1 more.
choice_feedback.C: Pencil C covers about 7 spaces. Pencil D is longer.
choice_feedback.E: Pencil E sticks out the farthest to the right, but it starts later. It covers about 8 spaces, and D covers about 9.

q03.key_idea: Check each face for 4 things: hat or hair, glasses or dot eyes, mouth, and ears.
steps: Each face has a hat or hair, glasses or dot eyes, a smile or an open mouth, and ears or no ears.
Look for each answer face in the big picture and count how many times it shows up.
Faces A, B, C and D each show up 2 times.
Face E has a hat, dot eyes, a smile and ears. Only one face in the picture looks like that: the 4th face in the middle row.

choice_feedback.A: The face with hair, dot eyes, an open mouth and ears shows up 2 times: at the start of the middle row and at the end of the bottom row.
choice_feedback.B: The face with a hat, glasses and ears shows up 2 times: in the middle of the top row and in the middle of the bottom row.
choice_feedback.C: The face with a hat, glasses, a smile and no ears shows up 2 times: at the end of the middle row and at the start of the bottom row.
choice_feedback.D: The face with hair, glasses and no ears shows up 2 times: 4th in the top row and 4th in the bottom row.

q04.key_idea: Count the small triangles row by row and find the empty white spaces.
steps: The big triangle has 4 rows of small triangles: 1, 3, 5 and 7. That is 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16 small triangles.
The gray ones are already there: 1 in the top row, 2 in the next row, 3 in the next and 4 in the bottom row. That is 10 gray triangles.
The white spaces still need filling: 16 - 10 = 6.

choice_feedback.A: Count again: there are 6 white spaces, not 5.
choice_feedback.C: Count again: there are 6 white spaces, not 7.
choice_feedback.D: 8 is too many. Only 6 spaces are still white.
choice_feedback.E: 9 is too many. Only 6 spaces are still white.

q05.key_idea: Follow each strip from one end to the other and compare the pieces.
steps: The 1 is just a short strip with one fold. It is the shortest.
The 2 and the 5 are folded the same way, just flipped. So their strips are equally long.
The 6 has a top, a middle bar, a bottom and a right side, just like the 5. But its left side goes all the way from the top to the bottom.
That long left side makes the strip of the 6 the longest.

choice_feedback.A: The 1 is the shortest strip of all.
choice_feedback.B: The 2 is as long as the 5. The 6 is longer because its left side goes all the way down.
choice_feedback.C: The 5 is as long as the 2. The 6 is longer because its left side goes all the way down.
choice_feedback.E: The strips are not the same. The 1 is much shorter than the others.

q06.key_idea: From the other side of the window, the pattern looks flipped left to right, like in a mirror.
steps: From outside, each row is seen backwards: left and right swap. Top and bottom stay the same.
Top row inside: black, white, white. From outside: white, white, black.
Middle row inside: black, black, white. From outside: white, black, black.
Bottom row inside: white, white, black. From outside: black, white, white. That is picture D.

choice_feedback.A: This is the pattern seen from inside. From outside it must be flipped.
choice_feedback.B: From outside the top left square is white, but here it is black.
choice_feedback.C: From outside the bottom left square is black, but here it is white.
choice_feedback.E: From outside the middle square is black, but here it is white.

q07.key_idea: All 6 ducks are lying on the floor, so the basket that did not fall has no duck in it.
steps: Count the ducks in the baskets: A has 2, C has 1, D has 1 and E has 2. That is 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 6 ducks.
Count the ducks on the floor: there are 6.
So every duck fell. The basket that did not fall has no duck.
Only basket B has no duck. It has 2 ladybugs, a frog and a rhino.

choice_feedback.A: Basket A has 2 ducks, but all the ducks are on the floor.
choice_feedback.C: Basket C has a duck, but all the ducks are on the floor.
choice_feedback.D: Basket D has a duck, but all the ducks are on the floor.
choice_feedback.E: Basket E has 2 ducks, but all the ducks are on the floor.

q08.key_idea: Start with a line that has the same shape twice.
steps: The first column has 2 smiley faces and adds up to 10. 5 + 5 = 10, so a smiley face is 5.
The last column has 2 hearts and adds up to 4. 2 + 2 = 4, so a heart is 2.
The bottom row is smiley + star + heart = 10. So 5 + star + 2 = 10, and the star is 3.
Check the middle column: heart + star = 2 + 3 = 5. It works!

choice_feedback.A: If the star were 1, the bottom row would be 5 + 1 + 2 = 8, not 10.
choice_feedback.B: The heart is 2. Each shape is a different number, so the star cannot be 2.
choice_feedback.D: If the star were 4, the bottom row would be 5 + 4 + 2 = 11, not 10.
choice_feedback.E: The smiley face is 5. Each shape is a different number, so the star cannot be 5.

q09.key_idea: The 5 pictures repeat, so count in jumps of 5.
steps: The order is sun, ghost, cat, moon, flame, and then it starts again.
Every 5th picture is a flame: pictures 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25.
Picture 26 starts again with the sun. Picture 27 is the ghost.

choice_feedback.A: The sun is picture 26. We need one more.
choice_feedback.C: The cat is picture 28, one too far.
choice_feedback.D: The moon is picture 29, two too far.
choice_feedback.E: The flame is picture 25, two too early.

q10.key_idea: Find the smallest and the biggest sum, then check every sum in between.
steps: The smallest sum is 1 + 2 = 3. The biggest sum is 4 + 5 = 9.
Every sum in between can be made too: 1 + 3 = 4, 1 + 4 = 5, 1 + 5 = 6, 2 + 5 = 7, 3 + 5 = 8.
So the sums are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9. That is 7 different results.

choice_feedback.A: There are more: the sums go 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 7.
choice_feedback.B: One is missing. The sums go from 3 all the way to 9, which is 7 results.
choice_feedback.D: The sums only go from 3 to 9. That is 7 results, not 8.
choice_feedback.E: There are 10 ways to pick 2 numbers, but some give the same sum, like 1 + 4 = 5 and 2 + 3 = 5.

q11.key_idea: From above you see each stack as one square, and the top cube with the little window shows which corner is which.
steps: The back left corner has a stack of 3 cubes. Its top cube has the little white window, so that is the top left square.
Next to it along the back are 2 more cubes: one on top in the middle and one on the floor at the right. From above, the whole back row is filled.
One more cube sits in front of the back left stack, in the middle row on the left.
Nothing else is in the box. So from above: the whole top row, plus the left square of the middle row. That is picture E.

choice_feedback.A: This shows a cube in the front left corner, but that corner is empty.
choice_feedback.B: This shows a cube in the front left corner, and it misses the cube in the middle row.
choice_feedback.C: This shows a cube in the very middle, but the middle of the box is empty.
choice_feedback.D: This shows a cube in the very middle, but the middle of the box is empty.

q12.key_idea: Dimitry must share exactly one shape with Anna, one with Bella and one with Che.
steps: Anna and Bella both have a square. Anna and Che both have a triangle. Bella and Che both have a star.
If Dimitry had a square, a triangle or a star, he would share 2 shapes with someone. So he has none of those.
He takes the circle from Anna, the heart from Bella and the diamond from Che.
Diamond, circle, heart is picture E.

choice_feedback.A: The square and the heart are both Bella's, so Dimitry would share 2 shapes with her.
choice_feedback.B: The circle and the triangle are both Anna's, so Dimitry would share 2 shapes with her.
choice_feedback.C: The star and the diamond are both Che's, so Dimitry would share 2 shapes with Che.
choice_feedback.D: The square and the triangle are both Anna's, so Dimitry would share 2 shapes with her.

q13.key_idea: Compare towers that are almost the same to find each block.
steps: Tower 3 has a triangle on top of the pink block and the green block. Tower 1 has only the pink and green blocks.
So the triangle is 20 - 15 = 5 high.
Tower 2 has only the triangle and the green block. Tower 3 has a pink block too. So the pink block is 20 - 13 = 7 high.
Tower 4 is a pink block and a triangle: 7 + 5 = 12.

choice_feedback.B: 13 is the height of the triangle and the green block. Tower 4 has a pink block, not a green one.
choice_feedback.C: The pink block is 7 and the triangle is 5. 7 + 5 = 12, not 14.
choice_feedback.D: The pink block is 7 and the triangle is 5. 7 + 5 = 12, not 16.
choice_feedback.E: The pink block is 7 and the triangle is 5. 7 + 5 = 12, not 17.

q14.key_idea: Andrew threw 10 more arrows than he started with, and each hit gave him 2 of them.
steps: Andrew threw 20 arrows but started with only 10.
So he got 20 - 10 = 10 extra arrows.
Each hit gives 2 arrows. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10, so he hit the target 5 times.

choice_feedback.A: 4 hits give 8 extra arrows. Then he could throw only 10 + 8 = 18.
choice_feedback.C: 6 hits give 12 extra arrows. Then he could throw 10 + 12 = 22.
choice_feedback.D: 8 hits give 16 extra arrows. Then he could throw 10 + 16 = 26.
choice_feedback.E: He got 10 extra arrows, but each hit gives 2. So it was 5 hits, not 10.

q15.key_idea: The bridge is the same length in both pictures.
steps: Top picture: 3 cars and gaps of 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 6 metres.
Bottom picture: 2 cars and gaps of 4 + 4 + 3 = 11 metres.
The top has 1 more car, and its gaps are 11 - 6 = 5 metres shorter.
So the extra car fills those 5 metres. Each car is 5 metres long.

choice_feedback.A: With 3-metre cars, the top bridge is 9 + 6 = 15 m but the bottom is 6 + 11 = 17 m.
choice_feedback.B: With 4-metre cars, the top bridge is 12 + 6 = 18 m but the bottom is 8 + 11 = 19 m.
choice_feedback.D: With 6-metre cars, the top bridge is 18 + 6 = 24 m but the bottom is 12 + 11 = 23 m.
choice_feedback.E: With 7-metre cars, the top bridge is 21 + 6 = 27 m but the bottom is 14 + 11 = 25 m.
